entities.title: Library API 0.3: typed values and outcomes
entities.summary: The typed layer every UTV library offers from 0.3: one immutable type per everyday value, plain results for total operations, Outcome<T> for partial ones, shared diagnostic codes and per-language naming.
consumers: The C#, Java, Python, Rust and TypeScript libraries under implementations/, which implement it
Application developers who call those libraries
guarantees: Types are valid by construction; TryOf (or Rust's of) reports a bad value as an outcome instead of raising.
Only partial operations return an Outcome (unique, multiple, none, unsupported, invalid); total operations return plain values.
ZonedIntent has no comparison operators; ordering it needs a TemporalContext with zone rules.
Diagnostic codes in §5 are shared by every library; messages are free text.
Names follow the naming table in §6, and each library's README records any deviation.
entities.compatibility: The 0.2 JSON layer (everyday-api) stays unchanged beneath it. Libraries are versioned independently with SemVer (VERSIONING.md, Implementation versions).

sources.symbol: 2. Total operations return values; partial ones return Outcome

relationships.description: The JSON layer it sits on.

entities.title: Everyday API 0.2: the JSON layer
entities.summary: Twelve operations on UTV JSON values (parseIso, formatIso, fields, add, compare, daysBetween, posixSecondsBetween, contains, overlaps, resolve, toZone, toOffset), with canonical builder shapes and utv-result/1.0 results.
consumers: The five libraries under implementations/, which implement it
The typed layer of each library, which is built on it
Application developers who work with UTV JSON directly
guarantees: Every library produces exactly the outcomes in conformance/operations/everyday.json; where the prose and the fixtures disagree, the disagreement is raised rather than resolved by picking one.
Builders and operations produce exactly the canonical shapes in the document.
Operations never throw for semantic outcomes, and never read the system clock, time zone or locale.
Native adapters make the caller name the intent and refuse values tied to the host's local zone.
entities.compatibility: Kept unchanged from 0.3 on, beneath the typed layer (docs/library-api.md, §7).

relationships.description: Every operation returns a utv-result/1.0 result.

entities.title: Text form (utv-text/1)
entities.summary: How UTV values look in code, logs and documentation: what ToString returns and Parse accepts, defined only where it is lossless.
consumers: The five libraries' parseText and formatText, and their typed ToString and Parse
Application developers who read and write values as text
guarantees: parseText(formatText(v)) == v for every value the text form can express.
Intervals use brackets, so an excluded end is visible; EDTF slash forms are accepted as input.
Exact second counts and EDTF qualifiers have no text form: formatText gives unsupported (no-text-form), and parsing a qualifier gives unsupported (unsupported-form).
entities.compatibility: An interchange adapter: it adds no kinds or properties, so it changes neither the specification version nor the wire identifier.
